title: Parish and Alibi
premise: In the fog-bound coastal town of Hollowmere, coroner Mirabel Eastwick is handed the case of Ada Voss, a woman missing for eleven months whose diary was found in the marsh — with entries written after her disappearance. As Mirabel investigates, she realizes the killer is feeding her clues, someone who has read every page of the police file and wants to be caught on their own terms. The trail leads to the Voss inheritance: a fortune in land rights that Ada's family has been quietly strangling each other over for decades, and to Mirabel's own late father, whose name appears in the diary. In the end, Mirabel stages her own death to draw the killer out, unmasking the town's beloved retired constable — who killed Ada to protect the secret that he, not her father, caused the accident that started it all.
about_author: Petra Joubert is the pen name of a former rural registrar who spent fifteen years filing death certificates in farming communities before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about small towns where everyone knows your name and no one knows your business.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Mirabel Eastwick performs an autopsy on a drowned fisherman while cataloguing, from habit, every grave in Hollowmere's churchyard. POV: Mirabel. Establishes her intimacy with the dead and her quiet reputation for seeing what police miss. Emotional beat: solitary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: A Diary Out of Time
chapters.summary: Constable Rhee brings Mirabel a waterlogged diary found in the marshes belonging to missing Ada Voss. The final entry is dated three weeks after Ada vanished. POV: Mirabel. The impossible date lands like a cold hand on her neck. Emotional beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: What the File Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Mirabel pulls the official Voss file and finds it suspiciously thin — pages removed, interviews paraphrased. Someone inside the system tidied it. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: first flicker of anger at institutional rot.

chapters.title: The Voss Land
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter through Ada's diary excerpts: the Voss family's contested marshland, worth millions once the highway comes through. POV: Ada (diary). Introduces siblings Edmund, Cressida, and Uncle Hal as suspects. Emotional beat: Ada's growing fear of her own family.

chapters.title: Grave Visits
chapters.summary: Mirabel walks the cemetery reading headstones against burial records and finds a plot bought in Ada's name two months before she disappeared — by an unknown purchaser. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: the killer isn't hiding; they're performing.

chapters.title: Edmund's Grief, Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Mirabel interviews brother Edmund Voss, whose mourning feels staged, his alibi too polished. He quotes details only the file would contain. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: the uncanny sense of being watched by someone who knows her moves.

chapters.title: Cressida's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sister Cressida shows Mirabel the family accounts; Ada had discovered embezzlement days before vanishing. POV: Mirabel. A motive surfaces — but it fits too neatly, like bait. Emotional beat: suspicion curdling into doubt of her own judgment.

chapters.title: The Constable's Kindness
chapters.summary: Retired constable Ambrose Pell, who ran the original investigation, offers Mirabel help with disarming warmth. He mentions her father, Tom Eastwick, unprompted. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: comfort that prickles.

chapters.title: Entry Forty-One
chapters.summary: Forensic dating confirms the post-disappearance diary entries were written in Ada's hand — or a flawless imitation. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: vertigo; the evidence itself is lying.

chapters.title: Tom Eastwick's Grave
chapters.summary: Mirabel visits her father's grave for the first time in years. His death, ruled accidental, shares details with Ada's disappearance. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: grief reopened, personal stakes ignited.

chapters.title: The Third Accident
chapters.summary: Mirabel reopens her private files on the three deaths she solved unofficially — all connected to Voss land transactions. Pattern confirmed. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: cold clarity; this killer has been working for years.

chapters.title: Uncle Hal Confesses
chapters.summary: Hal Voss, drunk, nearly confesses to something — then is found hanged hours later, ruled suicide. POV: alternating Mirabel/Rhee. Emotional beat: horror; the killer is erasing witnesses faster than she can find them.

chapters.title: Rhee's Doubt
chapters.summary: Young Constable Rhee privately admits the original file was closed under pressure from above. He risks his career to help her. POV: Rhee. Emotional beat: alliance forged in shared unease.

chapters.title: The Marsh at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Searching the marsh, they find Ada's hidden lockbox: deeds, photographs, and a second notebook — half burned. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: hope that immediately costs something; they've been seen.

chapters.title: Someone in the Archive
chapters.summary: Records room break-in; the original Voss statements are gone. Only three people had keys. POV: Rhee. Emotional beat: paranoia — the leak is inside the station.

chapters.title: Cressida Runs
chapters.summary: Cressida flees town with cash, then crashes on the coast road — brakes tampered, mirroring Tom Eastwick's accident exactly. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: recognition; the killer is quoting her father's death back at her.

chapters.title: Reading the Killer's Hand
chapters.summary: Mirabel realizes the diary's later entries contain errors only someone copying from memory would make — the writer knew the file, not the truth. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: intellectual triumph shadowed by terror.

chapters.title: Pell's War Stories
chapters.summary: Ambrose Pell recounts the old Voss case over tea, steering Mirabel gently toward Edmund. His kindness is a leash. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: gratitude she can't justify doubting — yet.

chapters.title: The Highway Papers
chapters.summary: The land's true value hinges on a route survey signed twenty years ago — witnessed by Tom Eastwick and Ambrose Pell. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: the past snapping shut like a trap.

chapters.title: What Ada Knew
chapters.summary: Reconstructed from the burned notebook: Ada found proof the original survey was falsified, drowning a rival claimant — the case that made Pell's career. POV: Ada (reconstruction). Emotional beat: Ada's courage, posthumous and damning.

chapters.title: Midnight Caller
chapters.summary: An anonymous note arrives quoting Mirabel's own autopsy notes verbatim. The killer has been in her office. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: violation; nowhere is safe.

chapters.title: Rhee Follows the Keys
chapters.summary: Rhee traces archive access logs and finds a signature that shouldn't exist — Pell's credentials, used after his retirement. POV: Rhee. Emotional beat: the ground tilting toward an unthinkable suspect.

chapters.title: Edmund Breaks
chapters.summary: Cornered, Edmund admits he helped hide Ada's body but swears he didn't kill her — Pell told him it was an accident they'd both survive. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: pity for a weak man complicit in everything.

chapters.title: Where Ada Rests
chapters.summary: Following Edmund's confession, they find Ada's remains beneath the pre-purchased grave — buried with care, almost tenderly. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: sorrow; even monsters mourn something.

chapters.title: The Town Turns
chapters.summary: News leaks; Hollowmere splits between defending its hero constable and demanding answers. Mirabel becomes the enemy. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Pell's Quiet Warning
chapters.summary: Pell visits Mirabel at home, reminiscing about her father, implying accidents run in families. Threat wrapped in avuncular warmth. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: fear finally given a face she must pretend not to see.

chapters.title: The Missing Night
chapters.summary: Mirabel reconstructs Ada's last night: she confronted Pell at the survey office; he chased her into the marsh. The 'suicide' of Hal covered the trail. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: the whole shape of the crime emerging.

chapters.title: Evidence That Isn't
chapters.summary: Prosecutors review Mirabel's case and find her key evidence compromised — planted flaws suggest the killer anticipated her methods. Her credibility collapses. POV: Rhee. Emotional beat: despair; the trap was built for her specifically.

chapters.title: Suspension
chapters.summary: Mirabel is suspended pending review. Stripped of authority, she works from her kitchen table among her father's old papers. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: humiliation transmuted into stubbornness.

chapters.title: Father's Box
chapters.summary: In Tom Eastwick's effects, Mirabel finds his copy of the real survey and a note: 'If anything happens to me, ask Ambrose why the river moved.' POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: posthumous handshake with her father.

chapters.title: The Plan
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Rhee devise a dangerous gambit: announce publicly that the last piece of evidence — the original survey — will be handed to state investigators at the marsh boathouse. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: terrified commitment.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: They stage the handover with a decoy envelope. Mirabel waits alone, visible and vulnerable, counting heartbeats. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: stillness before violence.

chapters.title: Ambrose Comes Home
chapters.summary: Pell arrives, unsurprised, almost relieved. He confesses conversationally — the falsified survey, the drowning, Ada, Hal — justifying each death as protecting the town's future. POV: Pell/Mirabel. Emotional beat: evil wearing a neighbor's face.

chapters.title: The Marsh Takes Sides
chapters.summary: Pell moves to kill Mirabel; Rhee's backup converges; Pell flees into the marsh he knows better than anyone. Chase through fog and sinking peat. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: breathless pursuit.

chapters.title: Low Ground
chapters.summary: Pell, wounded and mired, refuses rescue, reciting the names of the dead like a roll call. The marsh takes him as it took Ada. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: grim mercy; she watches him go and does not look away.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Churchyard
chapters.summary: Ada is properly buried beside the graves Mirabel knows by name. Edmund faces charges; the town begins its long reckoning. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: exhausted peace.

chapters.title: Vindication, Unsweetened
chapters.summary: Mirabel is reinstated; the state reopens the old cases, including her father's. Justice arrives late and incomplete. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: bitter satisfaction.

chapters.title: Last Entry
chapters.summary: Mirabel writes the final entry in Ada's recovered diary herself, closing the account the killer tried to author. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: reclaiming the narrative from the dead and the guilty alike.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Rhee asks how she kept going; Mirabel admits survival cost her the town's easy love and her father's clean memory. Some prices you pay anyway. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: honest reckoning without consolation.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Spring. Mirabel walks the churchyard adding new stones to her mental catalogue, including one that reads simply 'A.V., finally home.' She locks the office behind her. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: quiet continuation — the living going on among the named dead.
